architecture.product_repo: KeepLab-Relay (backend/** plus the enumerated Android attachment surface are writable in this milestone; everything else under app/ is read-only)
architecture.product_stack: Kotlin 2.3.21, Jetpack Compose + Material 3, Navigation 3, Hilt, Room 2.8.4 (KSP), AGP 9.2.1 — as extended by M2 (Ktor CIO client, a Keystore-backed session store, one unique WorkManager `note_sync` pipeline) and by M3 (bounded retry, manual retry, a persisted conflict record, a 7-day product Trash distinct from the sync tombstone). M4 extends it further only with the A7 attachment foundation, the backend binary path, the Android offline/upload/download path and the minimal attachment UX.

new_packages: data/attachment/** (the attachment domain: model, local store, import/storage, transfer coordination)
extended_packages: data/local/** (attachment entity + DAO, the direct experimental schema bump, attachment metadata queries)
data/remote/** (the attachment API client: config, upload session, chunk append, status, complete, download)
data/sync/** (the separate `attachment_sync` pipeline and its trigger seam, bounded attachment retry)
data/NoteRepository.kt (only if the attachment creation/removal boundary genuinely belongs beside the note boundary)
di/** (wiring for the attachment store, the attachment API and the attachment pipeline)
ui/editor/**, ui/note/**, ui/home/**, ui/settings/**, ui/trash/**, ui/navigation/**, ui/auth/** (tiny integration points only: attach, list, show state, retry, remove)
entry_points: KeepLabApplication.kt (only if an M4 wiring change is genuinely required)
MainActivity.kt (only if an M4 navigation integration point is genuinely required)
AndroidManifest.xml (only if genuinely required; a FileProvider is not expected to be needed)
gradle: app/build.gradle.kts (dependencies required by M4 only; the expected outcome is NO change)
gradle/libs.versions.toml (versions/libraries required by M4 only; the expected outcome is NO change)
android_under_construction.tests: app/src/test/** (JVM only; no androidTest, no benchmark, no device)
android_under_construction.explicitly_absent_from_m4: A8 multi-device hardening, A9 multi-account, collaboration/sharing, cloud deployment, release hardening, Tencent COS provisioning, camera/drawing/voice/video capture, audio/video/octet-stream/executable/archive support, multipart or cloud-presigned upload architecture, a production orphan scheduler, a push provider/FCM, a permanent background socket, account deletion, production email, Google/Firebase identity, room encryption claims, tombstone GC

backend_under_construction.location: KeepLab-Relay/backend/ (created by A2, extended by M2 and M3; PRESENT)
backend_under_construction.build_model: INDEPENDENT_GRADLE_PROJECT with its own backend/settings.gradle.kts and backend/build.gradle.kts
backend_under_construction.wrapper: the existing repository wrapper, reused as-is (Gradle 9.5.1)
backend_under_construction.stack: Kotlin 2.4.20 + Ktor 3.6.0 (Netty) · PostgreSQL via HikariCP + JDBC · Flyway migrations · portable Docker assets (untouched, not executed)
backend_under_construction.m4_additions: the server-configurable KEEPLAB_ATTACHMENT_* limit set with the D-13 defaults; the authenticated attachment configuration endpoint; the portable ObjectStorage abstraction with the FilesystemObjectStorage development reference driver; the attachment persistence model (metadata, upload session/resume state, content objects, quota reservations, orphan state) with new Flyway migrations after V3; the resumable upload session protocol with server-side byte/hash/MIME verification; quota reservation inside one atomic persistence boundary; account/note authorization derived from the JWT subject; same-account content deduplication that never bypasses quota or count; satisfied download; safe removal; the findOrphanCandidates()/cleanupEligibleOrphans() boundary; deterministic backend tests; backend/.env.example placeholders
backend_under_construction.backend_non_goals: no cloud provisioning, no Tencent COS adapter, no cloud credential, no real backend/.env, no multipart/cloud-presigned upload architecture, no production orphan scheduler, no audio/video/archive support, no collaboration/multi-account/push code

architecture.stack_repo: Google-Android-Agent-Development-Stack (Specification Compiler, Verification Layer, Evaluation Core / Auto-Finalizer, Hermes orchestration kernel)
architecture.hermes: pinned vgit.af90026 (2026.9.24) at /home/zhong/.hermes/hermes-agent; never upgraded, reinstalled or core-patched
architecture.guard: the same unmodified orchestration/hermes/evaluation_adapter/contract_guard.py, invoked by the same fail-closed pre_tool_call hook
architecture.note: M4 is a host-side backend + Android build/unit-test milestone. It provisions no cloud resource, uses no device, executes no Docker asset, and needs no live PostgreSQL.

m4_facts.metadata_upload_download_split: FORBIDDEN — one contract, one session, one pass
m4_facts.reviews_created: NONE (no Attachment Review, no Storage Review, no Upload Review, no post-PASS audit)
m4_facts.expected_gradle_change: NO dependency change is expected; app/build.gradle.kts and gradle/libs.versions.toml are conditionally authorized only so a genuinely required addition is not a breach by itself, and any addition must be recorded in the M4 report
m4_facts.room_schema: current 5 -> next clean version (expected 6) by direct experimental bump for the attachment structures; DEV_DATABASE_RESET_REQUIRED = YES; no migration chain authored; exportSchema stays false
m4_facts.backend_schema: new Flyway migrations after V3 (V4+) only as M4 requires; no production compatibility chain
m4_facts.quota: LOGICAL attachment bytes owned by the account; duplicates count; a pending upload reservation counts while active and is released on abort/expiry/failed initiation
m4_facts.content_addressing: SHA-256; the server verifies the uploaded bytes; the object key derives from account scope + verified hash; the user filename is never a path component
m4_facts.note_usability: INVARIANT ATT-1 — a pending/offline/failed/resuming attachment upload never blocks note use
m4_facts.transfer_pipeline: one separate durable `attachment_sync` pipeline beside the existing `note_sync` pipeline; no duplicate upload for the same attachment
m4_facts.push: FORBIDDEN — no FCM, no push provider
m4_facts.process_death: deterministic simulation only (persist Room state, destroy/recreate repository/pipeline objects, resume from persisted state); no adb, no Maestro, no UiAutomator, no device
m4_facts.live_postgres: not installed on this host -> LIVE_POSTGRES_INTEGRATION = SKIPPED_TOOL_UNAVAILABLE; never a blocker; no infrastructure is installed inside M4 and the transactional quota semantics are not weakened

guard.package_switch_semantics: The guard resolves its package dir as os.environ['HERMES_CONTRACT_PACKAGE'] or the built-in default. The hook subprocess inherits the Hermes process environment. Setting the variable for the Hermes process points the SAME unmodified guard at this package; no guard, hook or config change is involved.
guard.known_limitation: Hermes configuration, Hermes core and the hook allowlist live OUTSIDE the guard's source_root (/home/zhong/.hermes/...), so the guard's path lists cannot classify them. They are protected by an explicit hard prohibition and stop condition in this contract and in the M4 execution prompt, enforced by fail-closed operator discipline — not by the path list. Stated rather than hidden.
guard.write_intent_note: The guard's terminal write-intent extractor reads a literal '>' anywhere in a shell command as a redirect (MB-A1-003 / MB-A2-008 / MB-M2-006 / MB-M3-006). Drive the guard by files and read-only commands; never inline heredocs or payload-bearing shell text.

contract_notes.supersedes: nothing; the frozen P0B-CLOSE contract and the A0/A1/A2/M2/M3 contract packages remain active and unedited
